arxiv-2005-09610.title: Free2Shard: Adaptive-adversary-resistant sharding via Dynamic Self Allocation
arxiv-2005-09610.creator: Ranvir Rana, Sreeram Kannan, David Tse, Pramod Viswanath
arxiv-2005-09610.description: Abstract . Propelled by the growth of large-scale blockchain deployments, much recent progress has been made in designing sharding protocols that achieve throughput scaling linearly in the number of nodes. However, existing protocols are not robust to an adversary adaptively corrupting a fixed fraction of nodes.

arxiv-2103-02744.title: The Positive Mass Theorem with Arbitrary Ends
arxiv-2103-02744.creator: Martin Lesourd, Ryan Unger, and Shing-Tung Yau
arxiv-2103-02744.description: Abstract . We prove a Riemannian positive mass theorem for manifolds with a single asymptotically flat end, but otherwise arbitrary other ends, which can be incomplete and contain negative scalar curvature. The incompleteness and negativity is compensated for by large positive scalar curvature on an annulus, in a quantitative fashion.

arxiv-2103-07462.title: Rapid onset of the 21-cm signal suggests a preferred mass range for dark matter particle
arxiv-2103-07462.creator: Venno Vipp, Andi Hektor, Gert Hütsi
arxiv-2103-07462.description: Abstract We are approaching a new era to probe the 21-cm neutral hydrogen signal from the period of cosmic dawn. This signal offers a unique window to the virgin Universe, e.g. , to study dark matter models with different small-scale behaviours. The EDGES collaboration has recently published the first results of the global 21-cm spectrum.

arxiv-2201-07759.title: Tune-out and magic wavelengths, and electric quadrupole transition properties of the singly charged alkaline-earth metal ions Journal: Atomic Data and Nuclear Data Tables
arxiv-2201-07759.creator: Mandeep Kaur a, Sukhjit Singh a, B. K. Sahoo b, Bindiya Arora a
arxiv-2201-07759.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mandeep Kaur a, Sukhjit Singh a, B. K. Sahoo b, Bindiya Arora a. In continuation to our earlier reported data on the electric dipole (E1) matrix elements and lifetimes of the metastable states of the alkaline earth ions in [Atomic Data and Nuc. Data Tables 137 (2021) 101381], we present here the tune-out and magic wavelengths of the Mg + , Ca + , Sr + and Ba + alkaline earth-metal ions by determining dynamic E1 polarizabilities.

arxiv-2310-12466.title: Higher Level Completeness for Permutation Polynomials
arxiv-2310-12466.creator: S Rajagopal, P Vanchinathan*
arxiv-2310-12466.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S Rajagopal, P Vanchinathan*. Generalising the concept of a complete permutation polynomial over a finite field, we define completness to level k k for k ≥ 1 k\geq 1 in fields of odd characteristic. We construct two families of polynomials that satisfy the condition of high level completeness for all finite fields, and two more families complete to the maximum level possible for large collection of finite fields.

arxiv-2402-06393.title: Stellar streams from black hole-rich star clusters 2024 Stellar streams from black hole-rich star clusters – 12
arxiv-2402-06393.creator: Daniel Roberts, Mark Gieles, Denis Erkal, Jason L. Sanders
arxiv-2402-06393.description: Abstract Nearly a hundred progenitor-less, thin stellar streams have been discovered in the Milky Way, thanks to Gaia and related surveys. Most streams are believed to have formed from star clusters and it was recently proposed that extended star clusters – rich in stellar-mass black holes (BHs) – are efficient in creating streams.

arxiv-2407-19868.title: POREMAPS: A finite difference based Porous Media Anisotropic Permeability Solver for Stokes flow
arxiv-2407-19868.creator: David Krach, Matthias Ruf, Holger Steeb
arxiv-2407-19868.description: Abstract Abstract Porous materials are ubiquitous in various engineering and geological applications, where their permeability plays a critical role in viscous fluid flow and transport phenomena. Understanding and characterizing the microscale properties, the effective hydraulic parameters, and also the anisotropy of porous materials are essential for accurate modeling and predicting fluid flow behavior.

arxiv-2504-15141.title: Breaking Down Quantum Compilation: Profiling and Identifying Costly Passes
arxiv-2504-15141.creator: Felix Zilk, Alessandro Tundo, Vincenzo De Maio, Ivona Brandic
arxiv-2504-15141.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Felix Zilk, Alessandro Tundo, Vincenzo De Maio, Ivona Brandic. With the increasing capabilities of quantum systems, the efficient, practical execution of quantum programs is becoming more critical. Each execution includes compilation time, which accounts for substantial overhead of the overall program runtime. To address this challenge, proposals that leverage precompilation techniques have emerged, whereby entire circuits or select components are precompiled to mitigate the compilation time spent during execution.

arxiv-2509-09493.title: Weaker Assumptions for Asymmetric Trust
arxiv-2509-09493.creator: Ignacio Amores-Sesar, Christian Cachin, Juan Villacis
arxiv-2509-09493.description: Abstract In distributed systems with asymmetric trust, each participant is free to make its own trust assumptions about others, captured by an asymmetric quorum system. This contrasts with ordinary, symmetric quorum systems and threshold models, where trust assumptions are uniformly shared among participants.

arxiv-2512-02063.title: Dispersion Outperforms Absorption: EIT-Enhanced Atomic Localization and Gradient Sensing with Super-Gaussian Beams
arxiv-2512-02063.creator: Mahboob Ul Haq
arxiv-2512-02063.description: Abstract This work presents a comprehensive theoretical comparison between absorption-based and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT)-based atomic gradient sensing in a four-level tripod system. Both methods were evaluated under identical and optimized physical conditions to ensure a fair and unbiased comparison.

arxiv-2601-08444.title: Beyond Linearization: Attributed Table Graphs for Table Reasoning
arxiv-2601-08444.creator: Yuxiang Wang , Junhao Gan , Shengxiang Gao , Shenghao Ye , Zhengyi Yang , Jianzhong Qi
arxiv-2601-08444.description: Abstract Table reasoning, a task to answer questions by reasoning over data presented in tables, is an important topic due to the prevalence of knowledge stored in tabular formats. Recent solutions use Large Language Models (LLMs), exploiting the semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

arxiv-2602-17344.title: Invertibility of the Fourier Diffraction Relation in Raster Scan Diffraction Tomography
arxiv-2602-17344.creator: Peter Elbau peter.elbau@univie.ac.at, Noemi Naujoks noemi.naujoks@univie.ac.at
arxiv-2602-17344.description: Abstract Diffraction tomography aims to recover an object’s scattering potential from measured wave fields. In the classical setting, the object is illuminated by plane waves from many directions, and the Fourier diffraction theorem gives a direct relation between the Fourier transform of the scattering potential of the object and the Fourier transformed measurements.

arxiv-2602-23552.title: Diode Effect May Assist Finding Proper Superconductivity Mechanism in Copper Oxides
arxiv-2602-23552.creator: Armen Gulian, Serafim Teknowijoyo, Vahan Nikoghosyan
arxiv-2602-23552.description: Abstract We present measurements demonstrating that copper-oxide high-temperature superconductors can exhibit broken time-reversal symmetry in the absence of external magnetic fields. Using T ​ l 2 ​ B ​ a 2 ​ C ​ a ​ C ​ u 2 ​ O 8 Tl_{2}Ba_{2}CaCu_{2}O_{8} microbridges, we observe a pronounced superconducting diode effect at 100 K under strictly zero-field conditions.

pmc-11493019.creator: Chenhui Ma, Lei Gao, Kewei Song, Baohong Gu, Bofang Wang, Weigao Pu, Hao Chen
pmc-11493019.description: Background: To elucidate the mechanisms by which Jolkinolide B (JB), derived from Euphorbia fischeriana, suppresses gastric cancer (GC) development, given its known potent antitumor effects and the lack of detailed understanding of its impact and molecular processes in GC.Methods: The study utilized both cellular and animal models to investigate the effects of JB on GC.

pmc-11644185.title: Compare and Contrast of the Cellular Actions of Related Flavonoids, Apigenin and Chrysin
pmc-11644185.creator: Patrick Keefe, Prasanth Puthanveetil, Kai Wang
pmc-11644185.description: In this review, we provide an evidence-based approach to determine the cellular and systemic actions of two structurally similar flavonoids, apigenin and chrysin. We have clearly evaluated and charted the overlapping and diverging properties of these two sister flavonoids. Based on two separate Omics-based approaches by our group and independent reports from others, the cholesterol-lowering properties have been revealed.

pmc-11701435.title: The literacy barrier in clinical trial consents: a retrospective analysis
pmc-11701435.creator: Fatima N. Mirza, Eric Wu, Hael F. Abdulrazeq, Ian D. Connolly, Oliver Y. Tang, Cheryl K. Zogg, Theresa Williamson, Paul F. Galamaga, G. Dean Roye, Prakash Sampath, Albert E. Telfeian, Abrar A. Qureshi, Michael W. Groff, John H. Shin, Wael F. Asaad, Tiffany J. Libby, Ziya L. Gokaslan, Isaac S. Kohane
pmc-11701435.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryBackgroundHistorically, the readability of consent forms in medicine have been above the average reading level of patients. This can create challenges in obtaining truly informed consent, but the implications on clinical trial participant retention are not fully explored. To address this gap, we seek to analyze clinical trial consent forms by determining their readability and relationship with the associated trial's participant dropout rate.

pmc-12502105.title: Effect of Tai Chi combined with visual-action-sensory rehabilitation therapies on cognitive function in acute ischemic stroke: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12502105.creator: Xuewei Guan, Meijuan Lan, Lan Ge, Qianyin Zhu, Yuanyuan Chen, Leiwen Tang, Yumei Zhong
pmc-12502105.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionEarly cognitive intervention in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with better outcomes. ‘Visual-action-sensory’ rehabilitation therapies, including action observation therapy (AOT) and sensory observation therapy (SOT) have shown great potential in restoring cognitive function. A systematic review of some studies on the therapeutic effect of Tai Chi (TC)in stroke patients suggests potential benefits on depression, anxiety, and balance function. Therefore, combining AOT with TC may enhance brain functional connectivity and provide some cognitive improvements.

pmc-12753747.creator: Ziwen Lv, Qi Feng, Junhui Gu, Zhuo Gao, Dong Liu
pmc-12753747.description: Acute respiratory failure is a common disease, impacting various cancer survivors and reflecting post-surgery complications. pmc-12805675.title: Discrepancy in perceived appropriate and desired resuscitation durations between physicians and laypersons in cardiac arrest patients
pmc-12805675.creator: Yuko Tanabe, Takeshi Namba, Shoichi Maeda, Mitsuaki Nishikimi, Eri Ishikawa, Shinichiro Ohshimo, Nobuaki Shime
pmc-12805675.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study examined a discrepancy that exists between the duration of resuscitative efforts that physicians perceive as appropriate and the duration that laypersons desire. We conducted an online nationwide cross-sectional survey with 323 physicians and 2,667 laypersons. Physicians were significantly more likely than laypersons to consider a duration of ≥ 30 min as appropriate for resuscitation, especially in younger patients (age 0–6:85% vs. 27%; age 7–17:84% vs. 29%; both p < 0.001).

pmc-13036081.title: Design of an automated cell batch microinjection system based on magnetic tweezers for zebrafish embryos
pmc-13036081.creator: Xiangyu Guo, Fanghao Wang, Antian Zhao, Youchao Zhang, Huanyu Jiang, Alois Knoll, Meixiao Shen, Fan Lv, Mingchuan Zhou
pmc-13036081.description: Batch microinjection significantly enhances throughput and reproducibility in gene delivery and developmental studies, thereby accelerating the advancement of intelligent experimentation in the life sciences. In this work, we propose a novel visual-guided automated batch microinjection system based on magnetic tweezers, designed for zebrafish embryos.

pmc-13091770.title: Cold-press sintering and particle-size engineering of Bi0.3Sb1.7Te3 for enhanced thermoelectric performance
pmc-13091770.creator: Ruifeng Xiong, Jeremy Lemoigne, Aran Rafferty, Franck Gascoin, Amir Pakdel
pmc-13091770.description: SummaryMicrostructural engineering is a crucial approach to improving the conversion efficiency of thermoelectric materials and enabling their broad application. In this study, Bi0.3Sb1.7Te3 samples were fabricated via cold pressing, hot pressing, and combined cold/hot pressing, each followed by vacuum sintering, allowing for a systematic comparison of the effect of processing on thermoelectric properties.

pmc-13264365.title: A local vascularized scapula bone graft to treat posterior glenohumeral instability—an innovative surgical technique
pmc-13264365.creator: Philipp Lamby, Norbert Heine, Andreas Eigenberger, Christoph Eckstein, Lukas Prantl, Johannes Zellner, Paul Schmitz
pmc-13264365.description: BackgroundPosterior glenohumeral instability (PGHI) is a relatively rare functional disability. In cases of significant bony or soft tissue defects, surgical treatment is often unavoidable. Based on the type of defect, a soft tissue procedure, a glenoid reconstruction/augmentation with an allograft, or a combined surgical procedure must be performed.

uslaw-usc-t47-s765c.description: United States Code, Title 47 (Telecommunications); Chapter 6 (Communications Satellite System); Subchapter VI (Communications Competition And Privatization); Part C (Deregulation And Other Statutory Changes). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
